proposed_widenings.name: MagicItemRecord + magic_item mechanics family
proposed_widenings.justification: UnitRecord = SpellRecord | ClassFeatureRecord | MasteryRecord. There is no MagicItemRecord type. The v4 taxonomy defines magic_item_root as a source atom, but types.ts has never been widened to include the corresponding record or any mechanics family for magic items.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Wondrous Item, Uncommon — the unit is a magic item, a kind with no entry in UnitRecord.

proposed_widenings.name: ClassFeatureActivationCost.magic_action (or a parallel activation-cost type for items)
proposed_widenings.justification: The bottle costs a Magic action to activate. Existing ClassFeatureActivationCost only supports 'free' and 'bonus_action'. Magic action is a distinct SRD action kind that consumes the Magic action quota.
proposed_widenings.evidence: As a Magic action, you can open or close this bottle.

proposed_widenings.name: toggle_effect family (stateful open/close with two distinct persistent states)
proposed_widenings.justification: The bottle has a stateful toggle: open produces an active, growing emanation; close transitions the cloud to a fixed, slowly dispersing state. No existing mechanics family models a persistent object toggle where opening and closing produce distinct ongoing states with different lifecycle behaviors.
proposed_widenings.evidence: As a Magic action, you can open or close this bottle. Closing the bottle causes the cloud to become fixed in place until it disperses after 10 minutes.

proposed_widenings.name: Attachment kind: emanation_from_object (item-anchored sphere that follows the item)
proposed_widenings.justification: The smoke fills a 60-ft Emanation originating from the bottle itself — an item attachment, not self (creature) or a placed area. Current Attachment kinds are self | target | area | mark. None models an area that originates from and moves with a held/placed item.
proposed_widenings.evidence: forming a cloud that fills a 60-foot Emanation originating from the bottle

proposed_widenings.name: LevelAxis or scaling kind for time-based area growth
proposed_widenings.justification: The Emanation grows 10 ft per minute while open (60 ft → 120 ft cap). Existing LevelAxis values are character | class | slot | subclass | proficiency_bonus — none cover time-based (per-minute) growth. A new axis or a separate time-growth shape is needed.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Each minute the bottle remains open, the size of the Emanation increases by 10 feet until it reaches its maximum size of 120 feet.

proposed_widenings.name: apply_obscurement (or grant_heavy_obscurement area effect)
proposed_widenings.justification: The smoke makes the affected area Heavily Obscured — a vision-blocking environmental effect. The v4 taxonomy has block_targeting but no surface effect type represents granting obscurement to an area. This is mechanically distinct from block_targeting (which prevents targeting) and from any existing Effect variant in types.ts.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The area within the smoke is Heavily Obscured.

proposed_widenings.name: Duration or dispersal lifecycle: conditional_dispersal (time + environmental trigger)
proposed_widenings.justification: The fixed cloud disperses after 10 minutes OR after 1 minute in strong wind (Gust of Wind). No existing Duration or lifecycle atom handles a dual-condition dispersal (timer + named environmental event). The timed Duration in types.ts has no conditional-override branch.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Closing the bottle causes the cloud to become fixed in place until it disperses after 10 minutes. A strong wind... disperses the cloud after 1 minute.

notes: Primary stopper is structural: magic_item is not a valid UnitRecord kind. No Dhall or JSON can be authored — the tracer would throw on the root switch before reaching any mechanics. Beyond the missing record type, the item would require at minimum: a magic_action cost variant, an emanation_from_object attachment, time-based area scaling, a heavy-obscurement area effect atom, and a dual-condition dispersal lifecycle. The open/close toggle pattern itself (two distinct persistent states on one item) has no analogous family in the current schema.
